newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communists to discuss move to oust Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Communists to discuss move to oust Yeltsin.

text.p: The leader of Russia's communists said the party would decide on Thursday whether to support a parliamentary move to try to force President Boris Yeltsin from office because of ill health.
"I consider the initiative well-founded and completely understandable," Gennady Zyuganov, whose party is the largest in the State Duma lower house, told a news conference on Wednesday.

On the initiative of Communist lawmaker Viktor Ilyukhin, chairman of the Duma security committee, parliament's legal department began reviewing a motion on Tuesday to dismiss Yeltsin, 65, who is now in hospital recovering from pneumonia.
Ilyukhin is pressing for a Duma vote on Friday.
The Russian constitution is vague in describing the removal of a president for health reasons, and the current effort has virtually no chance of success.

"The president last year worked four months -- only during the election campaign -- and on the whole he didn't focus on government affairs but on promises," said Zyuganov, 52, who lost to Yeltsin in last July's presidential election.
"For any citizen of the country it raises the question: 'Why isn't there any leadership in the country?'" he said.
Doctors said on Tuesday that Yeltsin's condition had improved considerably in the elite Moscow hospital where he is being treated for pneumonia in both lungs.

But many observers have questioned whether he will have the strength to tackle the country's many problems after his recovery from pneumonia so soon after his quintuple heart bypass surgery on November 5.

"From a personal standpoint, I'm surprised that relatives, those close to him, friends, the president's circle, decided to finish him off by forcing him off to work after a serious operation," Zyuganov said.
Asked if he supported Ilyukhin's efforts to push Yeltsin aside for health reasons, the Communist leader said the party would make a decision on their stance on Thursday.
Gennady Seleznyov, the Communist chairman of the opposition- dominated Duma, said on Wednesday the party could not ignore the public's need for leadership during Yeltsin's absence.
Zyuganov on Wednesday also repeated criticism of a Yeltsin call on Monday to hold referendums on possible unification of Russia and the former Soviet republic of Belarus, a union he said he favours.

"The executive branch is working very poorly on the integration of Belarus and Russia," he said. "As I see it, they are suddenly acting on this (referendum) for one reason only: because on every other front they have failed completely."
He suggested that Russia's parliament and government should work together to seek unification with with Belarus as well as Ukraine.
